BiblicalUsage: Meli is honey, the sweet food of the wilderness and the picture of God's word on the tongue. Mark 1:6 and Matthew 3:4 both describe John the Baptist eating locusts and wild honey in the desert, and Revelation 10:9 and Revelation 10:10 have John eat the little book, sweet as honey in his mouth, but bitter in his belly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe honey tells the truth about God's word twice over: it is sweet to receive and it can be bitter to carry. My position is that a prophet eats the whole book, not only the sweet part, and the bitterness is part of the calling.
RelatedTopics: Prophecy; Enjoying God's gifts; Word of God
